Remaining example/coverage points:

1. The first Reverse example is all lowercase, so input and output are identical and the main transformation is not visible. Consider using the existing mixed-case scenario as the first example, retaining the all-lowercase case later. This makes both the uppercase conversion and lowercase preservation inferable immediately.

2. The advertised length range is 1..100, but the listed cases range from 3 to 34 characters. Add comparable public/hidden cases at or near the maximum with mixed cases and two-digit substitutions, plus a one-character boundary. This would check that longer valid inputs and expanded outputs are handled.

The full alphabet coverage requested by 5DN1L and jonas_melo is now present independently in tests and validators. All 12 listed outputs matched my local check.

Possible close variation: Letters to numbers
https://www.codingame.com/contribute/view/218614b767c1181b022edd0195ec98b3fd53e
Both replace letters with concatenated 1-based alphabet positions. That accepted task converts both uppercase and lowercase letters, while this one preserves lowercase letters and uses Reverse mode. This is a close neighbor, not an identical contract; please compare whether the case restriction creates enough distinction.

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: Quick and easy, obvious pattern, simple solution.
Nice easy warm-up clash, clear statement and example.

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: A quick brainteaser.

Goal
* Please add "<<This clash is in Reverse mode only.>>" at the beginning.

Stub generator
* Please add a write statement, e.g. write answer.

Cases
* Please remove the trailing newlines from the input for:
  • Validator 1
  • Validator 2
  • Validator 3
  • Test 4
  • Validator 4

* Test 1: Please remove the trailing newline from the *output*.

* Each test and its validator currently use the same inputs. Please revise them so that they cover the *same scenario* with *slightly different inputs*.

* Please use real English words and/or strings of randomly ordered letters instead of the first several letters of the alphabet for most cases.

* Please ensure that all letters of the alphabet, both uppercase and lowercase, are covered:

  • At least once across all tests.

  • At least once across all validators.

Thanks.
Also, it would be interesting if more tests were added to cover all letters. Currently, it only covers 7: A, B, C, E, H, L and O.
i did all taht except the sub generator i found an issue with it everytime i change somthing, i didn't understood hoe it works exactly. thank you

For the stub generator, you simply need to add a new line "write answer". I've just tested it, and there shouldn't be any issues with adding such a line. For your information, a write statement generates the default code demonstrating how the answer may be output.

The revised cases are better than the original ones, which is good. However, some letters are still not covered. Note that you're not limited to 4 pairs of cases; you can add more if needed (up to 25 pairs). So, would you please add the following cases:

* Test 5: QUeSTioNSquEstIOns

* Validator 5: ANsWErsanSweRS

* Test 6: lyYjhFkVPBFVvjMgxKDWwzJXZMGpRB

* Validator 6: UcDyCDqmQXkiJBhtFHjVGuLXjPZoqOvdTp

Thanks.
